<description>
Loading a snapshot checks the coins cache against -dbcache only every 120000 coins. A coin can carry a script of up to 10000 bytes. A snapshot file made of such coins can push the cache about 1.2 GB past -dbcache between two checks.

I added a check once the cache has grown by 4 MiB since the last one, and kept the 120000-coin check. Typical coins reach the 4 MiB bound about every 30000 coins. The added cost is negligible. Between checks the cache can still exceed -dbcache by about 4 MiB. I added a case to feature_assumeutxo.py that loads 2000 coins with 10000-byte scripts under -dbcache=4. It fails without the change and passes with it. The coins and validation unit tests pass.

This is one of several PRs from a large audit of Bitcoin Core that I did with the help of LLM tools. The audit produced its evidence all at once, which is why the PRs arrive together. I understand each change fully and will answer review questions myself.
</description>

<commits>
9bfcb7c15d validation: bound snapshot cache growth by bytes, not coin count

PopulateAndValidateSnapshot checks the coins cache against -dbcache
only every 120000 coins. That interval assumes small coins. A coin can
carry a script of up to 10000 bytes (MAX_SCRIPT_SIZE), so a snapshot
file made of such coins lets the cache grow by about 1.2 GB between two
checks, whatever -dbcache is. The file is only rejected at the end,
when the UTXO set hash does not match.

Also check the cache once its memory usage has grown by 4 MiB since the
last check. Typical coins reach this bound about every 30000 coins, so
the check runs more often for them too. Reading the usage is a few
additions, so the cost is negligible.

Add a functional test that loads 2000 coins with 10000-byte scripts
under -dbcache=4. Without the change the cache is never checked and the
test fails. With it the cache is flushed within 5 MiB of its limit.
</commits>

diff --git a/src/validation.cpp b/src/validation.cpp
index 9d1e1e3563..40c66984df 100644
--- a/src/validation.cpp
+++ b/src/validation.cpp
@@ -5811,6 +5811,10 @@ util::Result<void> ChainstateManager::PopulateAndValidateSnapshot(
 
     LogInfo("[snapshot] loading %d coins from snapshot %s", coins_left, base_blockhash.ToString());
     int64_t coins_processed{0};
+    // Coins vary in size (scripts can be up to MAX_SCRIPT_SIZE bytes), so the
+    // cache is also checked once it has grown by this much since the last check.
+    static constexpr size_t MAX_UNCHECKED_CACHE_GROWTH{4 << 20};
+    size_t cache_usage_at_last_check{coins_cache.DynamicMemoryUsage()};
 
     while (coins_left > 0) {
         try {
@@ -5851,11 +5855,11 @@ util::Result<void> ChainstateManager::PopulateAndValidateSnapshot(
                         coins_cache.DynamicMemoryUsage() / (1000 * 1000));
                 }
 
-                // Batch write and flush (if we need to) every so often.
-                //
-                // If our average Coin size is roughly 41 bytes, checking every 120,000 coins
-                // means <5MB of memory imprecision.
-                if (coins_processed % 120000 == 0) {
+                // Batch write and flush (if we need to) every so often: every
+                // 120,000 coins, or sooner once the cache has grown by
+                // MAX_UNCHECKED_CACHE_GROWTH bytes since the last check.
+                if (coins_processed % 120000 == 0 ||
+                    coins_cache.DynamicMemoryUsage() >= cache_usage_at_last_check + MAX_UNCHECKED_CACHE_GROWTH) {
                     if (m_interrupt) {
                         return util::Error{Untranslated("Aborting after an interrupt was requested")};
                     }
@@ -5872,6 +5876,7 @@ util::Result<void> ChainstateManager::PopulateAndValidateSnapshot(
                         // No need to acquire cs_main since this chainstate isn't being used yet.
                         FlushSnapshotToDisk(coins_cache, /*snapshot_loaded=*/false);
                     }
+                    cache_usage_at_last_check = coins_cache.DynamicMemoryUsage();
                 }
             }
         } catch (const std::ios_base::failure&) {
diff --git a/test/functional/feature_assumeutxo.py b/test/functional/feature_assumeutxo.py
index 8727a9925e..b178d4adb9 100755
--- a/test/functional/feature_assumeutxo.py
+++ b/test/functional/feature_assumeutxo.py
@@ -10,6 +10,7 @@ The assumeutxo value generated and used here is committed to in
 `CRegTestParams::m_assumeutxo_data` in `src/kernel/chainparams.cpp`.
 """
 import contextlib
+import re
 
 from dataclasses import dataclass
 from test_framework.blocktools import (
@@ -24,6 +25,7 @@ from test_framework.messages import (
     MAGIC_BYTES,
     MAX_MONEY,
     msg_headers,
+    ser_compact_size,
     ser_varint,
     tx_from_hex,
 )
@@ -166,6 +168,43 @@ class AssumeutxoTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
             msg = custom_message if custom_message is not None else f"Bad snapshot content hash: expected 106b2c56233e378a824cf0d5ff2be42ed32c72f1605c9be288d00942908a40ac, got {wrong_hash}."
             expected_error(msg)
 
+    def test_snapshot_cache_growth(self, valid_snapshot_path):
+        self.log.info("Test that loading a snapshot with large scripts keeps the coins cache close to -dbcache")
+        node = self.nodes[2]
+        self.restart_node(2, extra_args=["-dbcache=4", *self.extra_args[2]])
+        with open(valid_snapshot_path, 'rb') as f:
+            # Snapshot magic, version, network magic and base block hash
+            metadata = f.read(5 + 2 + 4 + 32)
+
+        # Each coin has a script of the maximum size the compressor keeps, so
+        # the coins cache grows by about 10 kB per coin. This is far fewer
+        # coins than the interval of coins between the cache size checks.
+        num_coins = 2000
+        script = b"\x51" * 10000
+        coin = ser_varint(1 << 1) + ser_varint(compress_amount(1)) + ser_varint(len(script) + 6) + script
+        large_snapshot_path = valid_snapshot_path + '.large'
+        with open(large_snapshot_path, 'wb') as f:
+            f.write(metadata + num_coins.to_bytes(8, "little"))
+            f.write(b"\x11" * 32 + ser_compact_size(num_coins))
+            for vout in range(num_coins):
+                f.write(ser_compact_size(vout) + coin)
+
+        log_start = node.debug_log_size(encoding="utf-8")
+        assert_raises_rpc_error(-32603, "Bad snapshot content hash", node.loadtxoutset, large_snapshot_path)
+        with open(node.debug_log_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
+            f.seek(log_start)
+            new_log = f.read()
+
+        # The cache must be checked, and so flushed, before it exceeds its
+        # limit by much more than the 4 MiB the node allows between checks.
+        sizes = re.findall(r"Cache size \((\d+)\) exceeds total space \((\d+)\)", new_log)
+        assert sizes, "the coins cache never exceeded its limit at a check during the snapshot load"
+        for cache_size, total_space in sizes:
+            self.log.debug(f"Cache size {cache_size}, limit {total_space}")
+            assert int(cache_size) - int(total_space) < 5 * 1024 * 1024
+
+        self.restart_node(2, extra_args=self.extra_args[2])
+
     def test_headers_not_synced(self, valid_snapshot_path):
         for node in self.nodes[1:]:
             msg = "Unable to load UTXO snapshot: The base block header (0c552ced4721c249a389eb9b08cb8da261cd46f0e7b5f9d064d48f3113406853) must appear in the headers chain. Make sure all headers are syncing, and call loadtxoutset again."
@@ -513,6 +552,7 @@ class AssumeutxoTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         self.test_snapshot_with_less_work(dump_output['path'])
         self.test_invalid_mempool_state(dump_output['path'])
